**Our understanding and proposed approach**

**What we understand**

Kilbride Veterinary Group runs three clinics in Navan, Trim and Kells, with 11 vets and 19 support staff. You take roughly 640 inbound calls a week. Orla estimates that about 38% of after-hours calls go unanswered or land on a voicemail nobody checks until morning.

Most of those calls are routine: appointment bookings and changes (about half), repeat prescriptions, and "is this an emergency?" questions. Emergencies must still reach the on-call vet immediately. Orla made clear this is non-negotiable.

You want an assistant that answers after hours, books routine appointments, sends reminders, and routes anything that might be an emergency straight to the on-call vet's mobile.

Your practice management system is VetLink 4. Orla confirmed it has no API. That means bookings will need a daily export/import file or manual entry by staff. We recognise this is not the smooth integration you had hoped for, and we will keep the handoff as light as possible.

You would like the system live before the spring vaccination rush in March 2027.

**What we propose**

We suggest a six-week pilot at Trim, your smallest clinic. This lets you test the assistant in a real setting before committing all three sites. If it works, we roll out to Navan and Kells.

During the pilot the assistant will:

- Answer after-hours calls and handle routine bookings and changes.
- Send appointment reminders.
- Triage "is this an emergency?" calls. Anything uncertain goes straight to the on-call vet's mobile. No voicemail, no delay.
- Pass confirmed bookings to your staff for entry into VetLink 4, or import them via a daily file, whichever suits your team better.

We will agree the exact triage rules with you and your vets before go-live, so the assistant never second-guesses a clinical call.

**To be confirmed**

- Budget. This was not discussed on the call. Orla will raise it with the two partners.
- Where call recordings are stored. We said we would come back to Orla on this. We will set out the storage location, retention period and access controls in writing before any recording begins.
- Client records include owner names, addresses and phone numbers. We will confirm how these are handled and protected once the storage question is settled.

Subject: Hybrid working policy – effective 1 January 2027

Dear all,

From 1 January 2027, Corrib Engineering Ltd will operate a hybrid working policy. Here is what it means for you.

**Who it applies to**
The policy covers employees whose role can be partly done remotely, as agreed with their line manager. If you are in your first six months (probation), you are not eligible. You work from the office full time during that period.

**Office days**
You must be in the Galway office at least two days a week. One of those days must be Tuesday, our team day. Your line manager agrees the second day with you.

**Core hours**
Whether you are at home or in the office, you must be available between 10:00 and 15:00.

**Getting started**
Hybrid working begins only after both of the following are done:

- Your line manager approves it in writing.
- You complete the home-office health and safety self-assessment form.

**Equipment and allowance**
The company provides a laptop and a headset. You may claim a one-off home-office allowance of up to €300, on receipts, for a desk, chair or monitor.

**What is not covered**
Travel between home and the office is not reimbursed. The company does not pay your home utility bills.

**Data rules**
Confidential client drawings must not be printed at home.

**Review and withdrawal**
The company may review or withdraw hybrid working for any employee or team. You will receive four weeks' written notice. This may happen if business needs change or performance drops.

If you have questions, email hr@corrib-eng.example.

Kind regards,
HR

**Q3 2026 Board Summary – Garden Centre Group**

Revenue across the three stores fell to €1,614k in Q3 2026, down from €1,630k the previous year. Gross margin dropped from 40.5% to 38.6%. The main cause is Store C (Athlone).

Store C revenue fell from €530k to €456k, a drop of €74k. Its margin fell from 40.8% to 36.1%. The finance manager puts this down to a national chain opening 2 km away in June 2026. Heavier discounting in August, aimed at holding footfall, accounts for most of the margin decline.

Stores A (Mullingar) and B (Tullamore) both grew revenue. Mullingar rose from €612k to €655k. Tullamore rose from €488k to €503k. Margins at both slipped slightly: Mullingar from 41.0% to 40.2%, Tullamore from 39.5% to 38.9%.

Online click-and-collect, launched in May, is included in each store's figures. It is not reported separately.

There were no one-off items in either year.

**To be confirmed:**

- The expected duration and severity of the competitor impact on Athlone.
- The specific cost of August discounting at Store C.
- Click-and-collect revenue and margin as a separate line.
- Q4 2026 forecast and any planned response to the Athlone situation.
- Net profit figures for the quarter.

**Subject: Client portal outage – Friday 14 November 2026**

Dear Client,

Our client portal was unavailable yesterday, Friday 14 November, from about 08:55 until 14:55. The disruption lasted around six hours.

**What happened.** A security certificate for the portal expired at 08:55. The automatic renewal had been failing since October because of a change in our website settings. We renewed the certificate by 10:40, but some browsers continued to show an error until the afternoon. The portal is now fully working.

**Your data.** No unauthorised access occurred. The expired certificate blocked connections; it did not expose any data. Our IT provider has reviewed the logs.

**Uploads.** Four uploads made between 08:50 and 08:55 did not complete. Those clients have been identified and will be contacted individually by Monday 17 November to resubmit. If you are not contacted, your upload went through.

**Deadlines.** The 14 November ROS filing for affected clients was completed by our staff by phone and email. No deadlines were missed.

**What we have changed.** We now monitor certificate renewals. Two staff members receive an alert 30 days before any certificate expires.

We apologise for the disruption.

Feeney & Walsh Chartered Accountants

**Office Manager – Gallagher Quinn Solicitors, Dundalk**

We are a small solicitors' firm in Dundalk. Three partners, four solicitors and five support staff. We do mainly conveyancing, probate and family law.

We are looking for an Office Manager to start in January 2027.

**The role**

You will run the office day to day. You will supervise our two receptionists. You will manage the diary system, file closing and archiving, supplier contracts, and IT liaison with our outside provider. You will also handle the accounts system for client money. Training is provided for this, but you must be comfortable with numbers and with handling confidential information.

**What we are looking for**

At least three years in an office management or senior admin role. Legal experience is a plus but not required.

**Pay and hours**

Salary: €42,000 to €46,000, depending on experience.

Hours: 9:00 to 17:30, Monday to Friday. One evening a week (Thursday) you will cover reception until 19:00 for late appointments. You get time off in lieu for this.

After a six-month probation, one day a week working from home is possible.

Pension arrangements are to be confirmed with the partners. Holiday entitlement is to be confirmed.

**How to apply**

Send your CV and a short cover note to careers@gqsolicitors.example by 5 December 2026.

Subject: Re: Brightwash laundry contract – what it commits you to

Dear [Name],

Thanks for sending this through. I am not a solicitor, so please treat this as a plain-English summary of what the contract says, not legal advice. Before you sign, I would strongly suggest you take the full document to a solicitor who deals with commercial contracts. They can check for anything the extract does not cover.

Here is what the contract commits you to:

**Length.** You are locked in for 24 months from 1 March 2025. After that it renews for another 12 months automatically, and again after that, unless you give written notice at least 90 days before each renewal date. Miss that window and you are in for another year.

**Exclusivity.** You must get all linen hire and laundry for the hotel from Brightwash. You cannot use another supplier during the term.

**Price rises.** Your charges go up each year by CPI plus 3 percentage points. There is a cap of 8% in any one year. The starting charges are not in this extract and are to be confirmed.

**Minimum spend.** You pay for 900 kg of laundry every month, whether you use it or not. In a quiet month you still pay for the full 900 kg.

**Their liability is limited.** If Brightwash causes you a problem, their maximum payout is what you paid them in the previous 12 months. They are not liable for lost business or lost profits, even if they deliver late.

A few things this extract does not cover and are to be confirmed: the base charges, what happens if you need to exit early, and how disputes are handled.

Please get a solicitor to review the full agreement before you sign.

Kind regards,
[Name]

**From:** [Name]

**Subject:** CRM replacement – recommendation

**Recommendation: Larchmont CRM (Option B).**

**Annual costs**

- Pipewell: €18 × 25 users × 12 months = €5,400, plus Zapier at €60 × 12 = €720. Total: **€6,120**.
- Larchmont: €29 × 25 users × 12 months = **€8,700**. No add-ons needed.

Difference: €2,580 per year in favour of Pipewell.

**Why Larchmont**

Gerard has confirmed the Xero link is essential. The accounts team re-keys every invoice today. Larchmont has this built in. Pipewell does not; it relies on Zapier, a third-party connector. If Zapier breaks or changes its terms, the link stops working and we are back to re-keying. That risk is not worth the saving.

Larchmont also includes a customs-document template. With Pipewell, Ciara would need about three days to build custom fields. The cost of her time is to be confirmed. Larchmont's vendor handles data migration. With Pipewell, we do the CSV import ourselves. The time this takes is to be confirmed.

**Trade-offs in Pipewell's favour**

Pipewell is €2,580 cheaper per year. It has no lock-in; we can cancel monthly. Four of the six staff who trialled both preferred its interface. Support is email-only during business hours, which is thinner than Larchmont's phone-and-email line, but may be adequate.

**Trade-offs against Larchmont**

The 12-month minimum commitment means we cannot exit early if the fit is poor. The interface was preferred by only two of six trial users. The price is higher.

**To be confirmed**

- Ciara's daily rate for the three-day setup (Pipewell).
- Hours needed for the CSV import (Pipewell).
- Whether Larchmont's phone support covers out-of-hours or weekends.
- Whether Pipewell's Zapier link carries any uptime guarantee.

**Conclusion**

The Xero requirement is non-negotiable. Larchmont meets it directly. The extra €2,580 buys a built-in integration, migration done by the vendor, a customs template, and phone support. I recommend we proceed with Larchmont.

Reilly Joinery, Cavan. Fourteen staff. Custom kitchens and wardrobes.

Before we got involved, every quote took about three working days. Fintan Reilly, the owner, priced each job from scratch in a spreadsheet.

We built a quoting template from their last 200 jobs. Standard units and finishes were priced in. We trained the office manager to use it. The work took six weeks and finished in September 2026.

About 70% of quotes now go out the same day. The remaining 30% — unusual layouts, bespoke finishes — still need Fintan and take about as long as before.

Fintan told us: "Most quotes go out the same day now. Not every job fits the template, and that's fine - those are the ones that need me anyway."
